stem: In which Winter Olympic sport do athletes race down an ice track lying on their backs, feet forward?
explanation: Skeleton racers use the same tracks but go headfirst, lying face down. Bobsleigh athletes ride inside a steerable sled instead of lying on top of it.

claims.text: In luge, athletes slide down the ice track lying on their backs with their feet pointing forward.
Skeleton athletes slide headfirst and face down, and bobsleigh athletes ride inside the sled, so neither lies on their back with feet forward.
Luge, skeleton and bobsleigh races are run on the same kind of artificial ice track.
A bobsleigh is steered by its pilot, and its crew sit inside it.

writerNotes: Subtopic: winter sports. lint: clean. claims: four, all standard. datasets: none applies. rivalTest: three options only, because there are exactly three Olympic sliding sports and a fourth (a non-sliding sport) would be filler (CONTENT_GUIDE §4, rule 9). Skeleton is the planted confusion: same track, opposite position. Argued against the key: no other Olympic event has athletes on their backs, feet forward. I avoided saying bobsleigh crews are 'two or four', since the women's monobob has a crew of one. volatility: evergreen. regional: Winter Olympics coverage is worldwide, though players in warm countries meet these sports less; the three options are the well-known names, so a player can reason from 'lying on top' and 'feet forward'. style: Oxford spelling ('bobsleigh'), explanation of 27 words. myths: screened. mystery and encore: not applicable. doubts: none.
